title: Best bank statement analysis tools for MCA underwriting: 8 options compared
summary: No single bank statement analysis tool is best for MCA underwriting; the right one depends on whether you need extraction or a decision-ready workflow, your deal volume and your team's technical capacity. This guide compares eight tools and gives you a six-step way to choose.
body_markdown:
### The short answer: match the tool to your underwriting job


No single bank statement analysis tool for MCA underwriting is best for every funder. The right pick depends on three things: whether you need extraction or a decision-ready underwriting workflow, your deal volume, and your team's technical capacity.


Quick picks by job:


- Self-serve analysis at a flat monthly price: LenderAnalyzer
- Enterprise document extraction through an API: Ocrolus
- Intake, scrubbing, and decisioning for funders: Heron Data
- Broker verdicts and lender matching: Zeneth UW Suite
- PDF-to-spreadsheet conversion only: DocuClipper or MoneyThumb converters
- Statement analysis that feeds automated decisions with credit, KYB, and fraud data: Lendflow Intelligence or Cevrynt


This guide covers why statements drive MCA decisions, the metrics that matter, and eight tools side by side. It closes with a framework for choosing.


‍


### Why bank statement analysis is the core of MCA underwriting


3 to 6 months of statements is the standard file, and 12 months is common for larger, seasonal, or renewal deals ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/merchant-cash-advance-underwriting) ;[ClearStaq](https://clearstaq.com/guides/bank-statement-analysis-guide) ). That lookback carries the decision because of how an MCA gets repaid.


An MCA is repaid as a fixed daily or weekly share of future deposits, so the statements drive the decision ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) ). Credit scores and tax returns add context. The deposit history tells you whether the merchant can carry the remittance.


#### The six metrics behind every MCA decision


Every tool on this list should calculate these metrics, or give you clean data to calculate them yourself.


- True revenue: deposits net of transfers, loan proceeds, and owner injections
- Average daily balance (ADB): the cash the account holds on a typical day
- Negative days: the number of days the balance sits below zero
- NSF and overdraft counts: returned items and overdrafts across the lookback
- Deposit consistency: how steady deposits stay across months
- Stacking detection: existing advances the merchant is still repaying


Gross deposits overstate capacity. True revenue strips out money that will never repay an advance, such as transfers between the merchant's own accounts.


#### Why stacking needs its own check


Stacking is a new advance taken while existing ones are still being repaid, and it is a leading cause of MCA default ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) ;[ClearStaq](https://clearstaq.com/guides/bank-statement-analysis-guide) ). The Secured Finance Network calls stacking "a fast track to insolvency" ([SFNet](https://www.sfnet.com/home/industry-data-publications/the-secured-lender/magazine/tsl-article-detail/strategies-to-overcome-merchant-cash-advance-(mca)-challenges-insights-and-solutions-from-industry-experts) ). A tool that misses an existing position misprices the whole deal.


Detection follows a clear pattern. Find fixed recurring debits, group them by funder, and total the daily burden ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) ).


‍


### Analyzer vs. underwriting platform: know which one you need


Most buying mistakes start here. Cevrynt draws the line clearly: analyzers extract, categorize, and calculate, while underwriting platforms go further ([Cevrynt](https://cevrynt.com/blog/bank-statement-analysis-software-vs-underwriting-platform) ).


Capability Bank statement analyzer Underwriting platform


Extract and categorize transactions Yes Yes


Calculate cash flow metrics Yes Yes


Business verification Typically not included Yes


Fraud signals Typically not included Yes


Policy rules Typically not included Yes


Decision-ready file Typically not included Yes


An analyzer fits a team whose underwriters make the call by hand. A platform fits a team that wants statement data to flow straight into verification, rules, and a decision.


#### Where Lendflow fits


Lendflow sits in the underwriting and decisioning platform category.[Lendflow Intelligence](https://www.lendflow.com/lendflow-intelligence) orchestrates cash flow data, business credit, KYB, and fraud checks, then applies your rules to reach a decision. If you only need PDFs turned into spreadsheets, a converter is the simpler buy.


‍


### 8 bank statement analysis tools for MCA underwriting


The tools below are grouped by category: converters and analyzers first, then platforms. The order is not a ranking. Pricing reflects only what each vendor or a named source has published.


#### 1. LenderAnalyzer: self-serve analysis at a flat price


LenderAnalyzer is a self-serve bank statement analysis tool built for MCA files. It fits small and mid-size funders that want analysis without an integration project.


Pricing is a flat $99 to $3,990 per month, per[LenderAnalyzer's own site](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) .


#### 2. Ocrolus: enterprise document AI through an API


Ocrolus is an enterprise document-AI and cash-flow-analytics platform that converts bank statements into structured data, delivered to lenders and fintechs through an API ([Zeneth UW Suite](https://zeneth-uw.com/ocrolus-alternative.html) ). It fits high-volume lenders with engineering teams that want extraction feeding their own models.


Pricing is metered per document, and rates are not published ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) ).


#### 3. Heron Data: intake to decisioning for funders


Heron Data covers intake, bank statement scrubbing, cash flow analytics, fraud, and decisioning for MCA, term, and SBA lending ([Heron Data](https://www.herondata.io/) ). Heron says it is "Trusted by 200+ funders, brokers, and fintechs" ([Heron Data](https://herondata.io/) ).


It fits funders that want one vendor from intake through decision. Pricing is quote-based ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) ).


#### 4. MoneyThumb: converters plus a fraud model


MoneyThumb sells statement converters alongside a separate analysis product and a fraud model ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) ). It fits teams that want to start with conversion and add analysis later.


Converters run about $25 to $100 per month ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) ). The analysis product is quote-based.


#### 5. DocuClipper: PDF-to-spreadsheet conversion


DocuClipper converts PDF statements into spreadsheets. It offers no underwriting analytics, so your team calculates every metric by hand ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) ).


It fits low-volume shops with spreadsheet-based underwriting. Pricing starts at about $39 per month ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) ).


#### 6. Zeneth UW Suite: broker verdicts and lender matches


Zeneth UW Suite is a self-serve tool for brokers that returns an MCA verdict and 30+ lender matches ([Zeneth UW Suite](https://zeneth-uw.com/ocrolus-alternative.html) ). It positions itself as an Ocrolus alternative for brokers.


Pricing is pay-as-you-go, with 5 free credits to start ([Zeneth UW Suite](https://zeneth-uw.com/ocrolus-alternative.html) ).


#### 7. Cevrynt: statement analysis inside an underwriting platform


Cevrynt is an underwriting platform where statement analysis feeds verification, fraud checks, policy rules, and a final report ([Cevrynt](https://cevrynt.com/blog/bank-statement-analysis-software-vs-underwriting-platform) ). It fits funders that want a decision-ready file over raw metrics.


Our research found no published pricing. Contact Cevrynt for a quote.

### How to choose an MCA bank statement analysis tool in 6 steps


Pick the category first, then the vendor. These six steps narrow the list fast.


#### 1. Define the job: extraction or a decision


Write down what happens after the statement is parsed. If an underwriter makes every call by hand, an analyzer is enough. If you want rules to approve, decline, or route deals, shortlist platforms.


#### 2. Model cost at your real deal volume


Per-document pricing compounds as volume grows, and verified public pricing for Ocrolus, Heron Data, and Prism Data is not available ([FintechSpecs](https://fintechspecs.com/blog/ocrolus-vs-heron-data-vs-prism-data-cash-flow-underwriting/) ). Request quotes based on your monthly file count and statements per file.


#### 3. Match the tool to your technical capacity


API-first tools need engineers to integrate and maintain. Self-serve tools work out of the box. Platforms with ready-made connectors and widgets sit between the two.


#### 4. Confirm coverage of all six core metrics


Check that the tool reports true revenue, ADB, negative days, NSFs, deposit consistency, and existing positions. A missing metric becomes a manual task on every file.


#### 5. Test stacking detection on known positions


Run files where you already know the existing advances. Confirm the tool finds each recurring debit, groups it by funder, and totals the daily burden.


#### 6. Map how the output reaches your decision and servicing


Ask where results go next: a spreadsheet, a credit memo, or a rules engine. Skip manual re-keying: pick a tool that hands results to your decisioning and servicing systems through an API.


‍


### Best practices for MCA bank statement analysis


Good tools still produce bad decisions when the process is loose. These habits keep the output reliable.


### Check for stacking on every file


Run stacking detection on new deals and renewals alike. Stacking is a leading cause of MCA default, so one missed position can erase a deal's margin ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) ;[ClearStaq](https://clearstaq.com/guides/bank-statement-analysis-guide) ;[SFNet](https://www.sfnet.com/home/industry-data-publications/the-secured-lender/magazine/tsl-article-detail/strategies-to-overcome-merchant-cash-advance-(mca)-challenges-insights-and-solutions-from-industry-experts) ).


### Keep every metric traceable to its transactions


Each number in a file should link back to the transactions behind it. Traceability lets underwriters verify a flag in seconds and gives auditors a clear trail.


### Benchmark on your own statements


Vendor demos use clean files. Test each finalist on a sample of your own statements, including messy scans, multiple accounts, and seasonal merchants.


### Pull the right lookback window


Use 3 to 6 months of statements for standard files. Move to 12 months for larger, seasonal, or renewal deals ([ClearStaq](https://clearstaq.com/guides/bank-statement-analysis-guide) ).


### Avoid underwriting on gross deposits


Gross deposits include transfers, loan proceeds, and owner injections. Underwrite on true revenue so the advance size matches what the business actually earns.


## Choose the tool that fits your workflow


The best bank statement analysis tool for MCA underwriting is the one that matches your job, volume, and team. Converters and analyzers suit manual underwriting. Platforms suit funders that want statement data feeding verification, fraud checks, and rules.


Start with the category, model costs at real volume, and benchmark on your own files. Then confirm the tool catches stacking every time.

### Frequently asked questions


#### What is MCA stacking, and how do you find existing positions?


Stacking is a new advance taken while existing advances are still being repaid ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) ). To find positions, look for fixed recurring debits, group them by funder, and total the daily burden.


#### Is bank statement analysis the same as MCA underwriting?


No. Analysis extracts, categorizes, and calculates metrics. Underwriting adds business verification, fraud signals, and policy rules to reach a decision ([Cevrynt](https://cevrynt.com/blog/bank-statement-analysis-software-vs-underwriting-platform) ).


#### Is Ocrolus a good fit for MCA brokers?


Ocrolus is enterprise document AI delivered through an API, so it suits teams with engineering resources. Brokers who want self-serve verdicts and lender matches may prefer Zeneth UW Suite, which positions itself as an Ocrolus alternative ([Zeneth UW Suite](https://zeneth-uw.com/ocrolus-alternative.html) ).


#### Can MCA underwriting be automated?


Yes. Platforms such as Heron Data and Lendflow Intelligence connect statement analysis to automated decisioning ([Heron Data](https://www.herondata.io/) ;[Lendflow](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/credit-underwriting-and-decisioning) ). Lendflow's rule builder combines cash flow metrics and document statuses into automated decision rules.


#### How much does MCA bank statement analysis software cost?


Published prices start at about $25 per month for MoneyThumb converters and about $39 for DocuClipper. LenderAnalyzer's top flat plan costs $3,990 per month ([LenderAnalyzer](https://lenderanalyzer.com/blog/best-mca-underwriting-software) ). Ocrolus, Heron Data, and the platforms here use quotes or unpublished rates, and per-document models compound at volume ([FintechSpecs](https://fintechspecs.com/blog/ocrolus-vs-heron-data-vs-prism-data-cash-flow-underwriting/) ).
